prompt: Eye-level view: camera 1.7 m above the promenade deck, looking along the Parade towards SpaceHQ, with people strolling. The Parade: a grand 40 m wide ceremonial boulevard with two-level shopping galleries along both sides (street-level arcades and a public deck promenade 9.4 m up, linked by curved stairs and bridges). A twin-beam coral-and-chrome monorail runs down the middle of the Parade at 24 m on slim pylons, with a sleek streamlined train. At the far end the Parade closes on SpaceHQ, a 250 m tall flagship tower of the space age rising from a round drum, the monorail entering the drum through a portal; rival spires with atom, starburst and saucer crowns stand beyond. A soaring glazed barrel-vault galleria roof of chrome ribs and pale glass spans the entire Parade above the monorail, like a space-age Galleria Vittorio Emanuele; sunlight falls through the glass in long stripes onto the promenade decks; the monorail glides beneath the vault. Optimistic retro-future atomic-age metropolis, the 1950s imagining the year 2000: Streamline Moderne, Art Deco and Googie on a heroic scale. Cream limestone and white enamel, seafoam-teal faience speed bands, coral-red fins and ribbons, brushed gold and chrome crowns, pastel peach and mint accents, rounded streamline corners, porthole windows, no glass curtain walls. Warm low late-afternoon sun, long soft shadows, warm cream haze on the far towers, soft blue sky. Clean, grand, prosperous civic city; no grime, no text, no signage lettering. Cinematic painted concept art with photographic material realism.
